newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices see mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices see mixed.

text.p: Gold prices in the Indian sub-continent are seen mixed with demand in India and Dubai rising with the festival season on while markets in Pakistan slow down, investors and dealers said on Monday.
"Things are looking up. The monsoon has now come to an end and India's (traditional) festivals and weddings are due to start in October," said one trader in Dubai.
Bombay traders said the season had already begun with last week's "Coconut Day" festival. Demand was expected to last for another two months.
The weekend seizure of 40 kg of unauthorised imported gold worth 20 million rupees by the Bombay customs is expected to see more inflows, which fell last week.

"Arrivals of imported gold may fall in the next few days after the seizure by Customs but if Custom resumes sale of confiscated gold then supply would be maintained," said Bhayabhai Sanghvi, former vice president of the Bombay Bullion Exchange. Customs routinely seize gold smuggled into India.

Gold prices in Bombay fell marginally by eight rupees per 10 grammes to 5,180 rupees in the week to Monday. Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) slid by 10 rupees at 60,640 rupees a piece in the same period.
Dealers in Pakistan's commercial city of Karachi said on Monday that Pakistan gold rates were poised to fall as investors switch funds into the dollar to hedge against the eroding rupee.

Local gold closed at 4,938 rupees per 10 grammes on Sunday compared to 4,930 on August 25, even though the Central Bank lowered the rupee rate to 35.6200/35.7981 to the dollar on Thursday, from 35.5300/35.7077 on August 13.
"Gold rates are likely to ease due to a liquidity crunch," said Karachi dealer Saeed Qureshi.

In Dubai, the main feeder market into India which is the world's single largest gold market, traders said the gold market was expected in the next few weeks to gradually recover from subdued summer business.
"We will start to see a gradual movement on the upside," he added.

While most Dubai traders were optimistic about a rise in demand from India in the near term, one said Pakistan did not have much to offer. "Pakistan is slow. The money market is a little bit tight," he said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $=35.62 Pakistani rupees, 35.65 Indian rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices September 2 & 26, Karachi and Dubai September 1 and 25 respectively.
